done.why: After a few minutes I was just walking through rooms and picking things up with no clear goal or puzzle pulling me in. It felt like a Zork rerun, so I quit.

about: A Zork-style cave treasure hunt south of a ravine. A Wizard haunts the caverns and the Empire's lost treasures are hidden further in.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared, hinted at where the treasures were, and made me drop the lamp.
The garden had a nice cozy feel after the dark tunnel.
I had no idea where the stone door with the question was.
The unicorn showed up and my sword glowed near it.

wished: A hint about where the stone door with the pearls was.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question, and the rest further in, past a room that will not keep still.
lines.why: This was the only line that gave me a goal.

fun.why: It was competent and familiar, but nothing grabbed me quickly.

engagement.why: I drifted through rooms without anything pulling me on.

difficulty.why: There was no friction in the few minutes I played.

interestingness.why: The Wizard's hint and the newspaper set up a quest, but I didn't follow it up.

prose.why: The prose was clean, with nice touches like the Wizard's look and the garden.
